task: Primary-source verification of particle-transport references in the attached Scopus AI report
scope_note: Literature provides motivation and context only. Retain Makhmudov et al. (2017) seven-saturation, fixed-deposit-porosity model; alter deposition kinetics only. Simultaneous deposition modes and pore-scale mechanisms do not establish the proposed temporal piecewise regimes.

references.title: Pore-network modeling of colloid transport and retention considering surface deposition, hydrodynamic bridging, and straining
references.access: Author-institution record and author-agency technical abstract verified; publisher open attempted, 403; full paper not inspected.
references.finding: The pore-network model distinguishes surface deposition, hydrodynamic bridging and straining. Bridging and straining generated hyperexponential retention profiles, while modeled surface deposition produced exponential or uniform profiles; bridging became relatively more important with increasing colloid size, concentration and flow velocity.
references.relevance: Include as pore-to-continuum context showing why a single effective deposition coefficient need not represent every loading condition. Do not assert its mechanisms or threshold values directly calibrate the proposed piecewise closure.

references.title: Physical experiment and pore-scale investigation of the clogging of polydisperse particles in saturated porous media during artificial groundwater recharge
references.access: Publisher-indexed abstract, metadata and highlights verified via search; direct open attempted, 403; full paper not inspected.
references.finding: Sand-column and SEM observations showed that three separately injected polydisperse size distributions produced different retention and clogging patterns. The smallest distribution produced more uniform deposition, while larger distributions produced hyperexponential retained profiles; deposition favored concave grain-surface regions.
references.relevance: Include as recent experimental evidence that particle size and local morphology affect loading-dependent clogging. Three separate size-distribution experiments must not be described as a simultaneous binary mixture experiment.

references.title: Modeling of retention and re-entrainment of mono- and poly-disperse particles: Effects of hydrodynamics, particle size and interplay of different-sized particles retention
references.access: Publisher-indexed abstract and metadata verified; publisher direct open 403 and HAL document unavailable. Full paper not inspected.
references.finding: An irreversible–reversible retention model was used to interpret experiments with 3, 10 and 16 micrometre latex particles and their mixture. Deposition and re-entrainment rates increased with velocity and/or size, and larger retained particles were proposed to suppress smaller-particle re-entrainment and provide extra attachment sites.
references.relevance: Strong support for component-specific kinetic parameters and interactions among differently sized particles. Its reversible/irreversible mechanism is an alternative closure, not evidence for sequential charging, transition and aging thresholds.

references.title: Effects of Particle Size Non-Uniformity on Transport and Retention in Saturated Porous Media
references.access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata verified; subscription full text not inspected.
references.finding: Short-pulse tests compared monodisperse 3, 10 and 16 micrometre latex particles with their mixture. Larger retained particles increased retention of 3 micrometre particles, while straining of larger particles was lower in mixtures than in monodisperse tests; the authors related the deposition coefficient jointly to size and flow velocity.
references.relevance: Direct support for binary/polydisperse transport motivation and component-specific kinetic behavior.
references.bibliographic_correction: Use pages 85–98, verified on Springer. Some derivative bibliographies incorrectly report 1–14.

references.title: Insight into particle retention and clogging in porous media; a pore scale study using lattice Boltzmann method
references.access: Publisher-version full paper in Utrecht University repository inspected, including abstract and model assumptions.
references.finding: Lattice Boltzmann simulations on six geometries showed how initial porosity and pore connectivity influence clogging and permeability loss. Their fitted porosity–permeability relations depended on geometry and topology, showing that porosity alone does not uniquely determine permeability.
references.relevance: Include as pore-scale context for hydraulic consequences of accumulated deposits, without changing the inherited permeability law.
references.limitation: Moving particles do not alter fluid properties or flow before deposition; particle interactions, gravity, van der Waals and electric double-layer forces were omitted, with attachment assumed favorable near grain surfaces. Do not describe this study as an explicit complete colloidal-force model.

references.title: Particulate transport in porous media at pore-scale. Part 2: CFD-DEM and colloidal forces
references.access: Publisher-indexed abstract and highlights verified; direct publisher access returned 403 and HAL access denied. Full paper not inspected.
references.finding: The four-way coupled unresolved–resolved CFD–DEM framework was augmented with colloidal interactions to investigate charged-particle transport and retention by aggregation. The indexed highlights specify DLVO forces, adhesive JKR contacts, and pore clogging associated with aggregation, deposition and remobilization.
references.relevance: Include with Part 1 as recent mechanistic pore-scale modeling context. It motivates effective kinetic descriptions but does not establish or calibrate the present macroscopic stages.

references.title: Particulate transport in porous media at pore-scale. Part 1: Unresolved-resolved four-way coupling CFD-DEM
references.access: Complete publisher-indexed abstract, metadata and highlights verified; direct publisher open 403, HAL denied. Full paper not inspected.
references.finding: A CFD–DEM method combining resolved and unresolved coupling was developed for particles moving through complex pore geometry, and checked against analytical or experimental reference cases. It was applied to pore clogging and permeability reduction due to particle sieving and bridging.
references.relevance: Include with Part 2 for current pore-scale computational context.
references.bibliographic_note: Part 1 has 2025 issue year despite DOI containing 2024; Part 2 has 2024 issue year. Preserve these publisher issue dates.

references.title: Application of a dual deposition mode model to evaluate transport of Escherichia coli D21 in porous media
references.finding: Controlled E. coli D21 column experiments revealed retained profiles inconsistent with classical filtration theory, especially at lower ionic strength. A discrete fast/slow deposition model described much of the retained profile but underestimated inlet retention and disagreed with released-cell fractions, indicating additional interactions beyond classical DLVO theory.
references.relevance: Include as both evidence for kinetic heterogeneity and a warning that a more flexible closure alone does not uniquely identify mechanisms. Fast/slow modes are simultaneous subpopulations, not temporal stages.

references.title: Deviation from the Classical Colloid Filtration Theory in the Presence of Repulsive DLVO Interactions
references.access: Author-posted publisher-version full paper inspected, including theory and conclusions.
references.finding: Uniform-particle and uniform-collector experiments deviated from classical filtration theory under repulsive electrostatic conditions. A distribution combining simultaneous fast and slow deposition described effluent concentrations, retained profiles and elution fractions more successfully than a single constant deposition coefficient.
references.relevance: Include in the discussion of limits of constant-rate kinetic descriptions. The paper deliberately minimizes blocking and ripening effects: its dual modes are not evidence for temporal loading stages.

references.title: Spatial Distributions of Cryptosporidium Oocysts in Porous Media: Evidence for Dual Mode Deposition
references.access: Author-posted publisher-version full paper inspected; publisher abstract and metadata verified.
references.finding: Retained Cryptosporidium oocyst profiles under unfavorable interactions departed from classical filtration predictions, which overestimated removal. A simultaneous fast/slow deposition model reproduced retained profiles and effluent concentrations; release behavior suggested additional oocyst-surface-specific interactions.
references.relevance: Include with the 2004 and 2006 papers to demonstrate scope and limitations of dual deposition modes, carefully distinguished from temporal multistage kinetics.

references.title: Stochastic model for filtration by porous materials
references.access: Publisher abstract and metadata inspected; full article requires subscription and was not inspected.
references.finding: The stochastic model couples statistically distributed pore-scale displacements and velocities with random attachment events governed by flow, pore size and attachment rate. It predicts generally nonexponential deposition profiles from the underlying disorder distributions.
references.relevance: Include as an alternative upscaling explanation for nonclassical deposition. Such spatial and transport heterogeneity must not be equated with a demonstrated temporal sequence of deposit maturation.

references.title: A Stochastic Model for Colloid Transport and Deposition
references.access: Publisher-version full paper at author agency inspected, including transport model and conclusions.
references.finding: A stochastic extension of the advection–dispersion model with first-order deposition and release explored variations and correlations in deposition rates, release rates and pore-water velocity. Several heterogeneity mechanisms generated hyperexponential profiles, while colloid chemical heterogeneity alone did not explain the tested data set.
references.relevance: Include to support mechanistic caution and distinguish rate distributions or two-region formulations from a sequential loading-dependent law.

references.title: Influence of particle contact mechanics parameters on deposition behavior and filtration performance in fiber filtration
references.access: Publisher-indexed abstract and metadata inspected; direct publisher open 403; full paper not inspected.
references.finding: DEM–CFD simulations linked rolling resistance, surface energy and particle size to evolving deposit structures and the transition from deep to surface filtration. The application is airborne particulate capture in fibrous air filters.
references.relevance: Recommend exclude from this aqueous granular deep-bed filtration introduction as peripheral. If retained, explicitly identify it as a cross-domain analogy; it cannot validate aqueous two-component kinetics or justify modifying fixed deposit porosities.

recommended_synthesis: Use Hammadi 2017 and Ma 2017 to establish that mixed-size suspensions show interactions that cannot always be inferred from separate monodisperse tests, motivating component-specific deposition parameters.

Use Tufenkji–Elimelech 2004/2005 and Tufenkji 2006 to establish limits of a single constant-rate classical closure, while explicitly distinguishing simultaneous fast/slow populations from temporal loading stages.
Use Bradford–Toride 2007 and Miele–de Anna–Dentz 2019 to show alternative stochastic explanations and avoid claiming nonexponential profiles uniquely prove temporal multistage deposition.

Use Lin 2021, Parvan 2020, Maya Fogouang Part 1/2 and Niu 2024 as pore-scale/experimental context for competing capture mechanisms and hydraulic feedback, without expanding the inherited Makhmudov framework.
Omit Jin 2026 airborne fibrous filtration unless a brief clearly labeled cross-domain comparison is essential.
